profile.summary: ProtGPT2 is a protein language model for designing new protein sequences. It reads amino acid sequence text and generates further sequence, either from a start token alone or continuing a fragment the user supplies. The developers report that the sequences it writes keep the amino acid composition and secondary structure content of natural proteins while sitting in parts of protein space that known proteins do not cover. The same model can score an existing sequence by perplexity, and ProteinGym lists it as a single-sequence baseline in its zero-shot substitution benchmark.

summary_quotes.text: we describe ProtGPT2, a language model trained on the protein space that generates de novo protein sequences following the principles of natural ones
ProtGPT2 generated sequences conserve natural proteins' critical features (amino acid propensities, secondary structural content, and globularity) while exploring unseen regions of the protein space.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: ProtGPT2 uses the GPT2 Transformer architecture. It is a decoder-only model with 36 layers and a model dimension of 1280. It was trained with a causal language modelling objective: predict the next token from the tokens before it. Sequences are split into tokens by a byte pair encoding vocabulary trained on Swiss-Prot, so one token is a short run of amino acids rather than a single residue, and the card gives an average of four amino acids per token. Pre-training used the raw UniRef50 sequences with the FASTA headers removed.
sections.source_locator: Model card: Model description; paper: Methods, Vocabulary encoding

quotes.text: ProtGPT2 is based on the GPT2 Transformer architecture and contains 36 layers with a model dimensionality of 1280
ProtGPT2 was trained using a causal modelling objective, in which the model is trained to predict the next token (or, in this case, oligomer) in the sequence.
BPE is a sub-word tokenization algorithm that finds the most frequently used word roots
length is expressed in tokens, where each token has an average length of 4 amino acids
The pre-training was done on the raw sequences without FASTA headers.

sections.title: What the developers use it for
sections.body: The card describes three uses. The first is generation with no further training: give the start token or a fragment and sample continuations. The second is fine-tuning on a user's own sequence set with the Hugging Face run_clm.py script, so that generated sequences follow that set. The third is ranking candidate sequences by perplexity. The developers report that perplexity values correlate with AlphaFold2 pLDDT, and advise sampling many sequences and keeping those with the lowest perplexity. They state that they have no threshold separating a good from a bad perplexity value.
sections.source_locator: Model card: How to use ProtGPT2; Example 2; How to select the best sequences

quotes.text: It can be used to generate sequences in a zero-shot fashion or to generate sequences of a particular type after finetuning on a user-defined dataset.
We've observed that perplexity values correlate with AlphaFold2's plddt.
the best is to sample many sequences, order them by perplexity, and select those with the lower values
We do not yet have a threshold as to what perplexity value gives a 'good' or 'bad' sequence

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: One checkpoint is released, nferruz/ProtGPT2 on Hugging Face, with weights also deposited on Zenodo according to the paper's data availability note. The file listing at revision ff981fc9 holds a single PyTorch weights file, pytorch_model.bin, of about 3.13 GB, plus the tokenizer files. The card now carries a notice that the same group has released ProtGPT3 and recommends moving to the newer models. A reported result should name the Hugging Face revision; this page read revision ff981fc96771d6f6d3b6453f94772d3cb6c7b90b.

run_guide.summary: Install transformers, then generate ten sequences from the released checkpoint with the example the model card gives.
prerequisites: Python with the Hugging Face transformers package; the card links its installation page for the details.
PyTorch, since the only weights file in the repository is pytorch_model.bin.
About 3.13 GB of disk for the weights file, as the Hugging Face file listing gives its size.
No GPU requirement is stated by the sources for inference. The paper's training used 128 NVIDIA A100 GPUs, which is a training figure, not an inference one.

steps.title: Generate ten sequences from the released checkpoint
steps.shell:
python3 - <<'PY'
from transformers import pipeline
protgpt2 = pipeline('text-generation', model="nferruz/ProtGPT2")
sequences = protgpt2("<|endoftext|>", max_length=100, do_sample=True, top_k=950, repetition_penalty=1.2, num_return_sequences=10, eos_token_id=0)
for seq in sequences:
    print(seq)
PY
steps.explanation: This is the card's Example 1, wrapped in a shell heredoc. The interactive prompts were removed and the card's stray colon after print(seq) dropped so the block runs as a script. The pipeline call downloads the weights on first use. Length is counted in tokens, not residues.

quotes.text: protgpt2 = pipeline('text-generation', model="nferruz/ProtGPT2")
sequences = protgpt2("<|endoftext|>", max_length=100, do_sample=True, top_k=950, repetition_penalty=1.2, num_return_sequences=10, eos_token_id=0)
length is expressed in tokens, where each token has an average length of 4 amino acids

outputs: One dictionary per sampled sequence, each with a generated_text field holding the amino acid sequence, printed to standard output.
To rank candidates, the card gives a calculatePerplexity function that returns math.exp(loss) for a sequence formatted with <|endoftext|> markers and a newline every 60 amino acids.
limitations: These commands were read from the model card and have not been executed by Rewire.
The sources give no pinned transformers version for inference; the paper names version 4.14.1 for training only.
No hardware requirement for inference is stated by the sources.

notes: Licence conflict to resolve by hand: the LICENSE file in the Hugging Face repository is MIT, while the card's own metadata and the Hugging Face API cardData say apache-2.0. The structured row records MIT, from the licence file, and both are stated in the Weights licence fact. There is no code repository for ProtGPT2, so the page rests on the model card and the paper. The card announces ProtGPT3 and recommends it over ProtGPT2; the ProtGPT3 preprint is on bioRxiv at https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.06.04.730041v1 and was not fetched, because bioRxiv is rate-limiting this address today. The Hugging Face createdAt field (2022-03-07) is a repository creation date, not a stated release date, so structured.released is null.
